That’s why I’m here, I think.\n\nDoctor: What makes you certain that your family is hiding your money?\n\nPatient: I mean… I know it sounds like I’m being hard on them, and I don’t want you to think I’m just trying to accuse people. But it’s been going on for more than a year.\n\nThey keep showing me bank papers and saying, “See, nothing was taken,” but that doesn’t feel like the whole truth. The money keeps getting explained away with bills, or some fundraiser, or plans for a trip, and it’s always like there’s a reason I shouldn’t ask too much. So I keep asking, because I feel like if I don’t, they’ll just keep covering it up.\n\nI know they say the papers prove it, but I’m certain they’re hiding it. I just need them to admit it. Is that… does that make sense what I’m saying?\n\nDoctor: Have you been having periods where you feel unusually energetic and need much less sleep than usual?\n\nPatient: Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I have nights where I don’t sleep great, but not like I’m full of energy or anything. I haven’t really noticed that. Is that okay?\n\nDoctor: Have you heard voices when no one else was there?\n\nPatient: No… I don’t think so. Not like hearing someone talking when nobody’s there. I mean, sometimes I get worried or I think about things a lot, but I haven’t noticed voices like that. Is that what you mean?\n\nDoctor: Besides the issue with your money, have you had any other strong beliefs that other people say aren’t true?\n\nPatient: Not really anything else… I mean, not like a whole separate thing. It’s mostly this money situation.\n\nI know my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, and I’m trying to hear them, I am. But for over a year it’s felt clear to me that they’re hiding it somehow. But I don’t think I have other beliefs like that… at least not that I can think of. Is that an okay answer?\n\nDoctor: Have you had any major medical or neurological illness?\n\nPatient: Um… no, I don’t think so. I mean, nothing major that I know of. I haven’t had, like, a serious brain thing or anything… at least nobody’s told me that. Is that what you mean?\n\nDoctor: Have you found yourself feeling much less interested in seeing people or doing things you used to enjoy?\n\nPatient: Um… I don’t think so, not in a big way. I mean, I maybe keep to myself sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I stopped liking people or things. I’m not sure if I’m answering that right.\n\nDoctor: Do people ever tell you that your speech is hard to follow or that your thoughts seem jumbled?\n\nPatient: No… I don’t think people say that to me. I mean, maybe if I’m upset I talk a lot or repeat myself some, but I don’t think my thoughts are jumbled. I try to explain it clearly. Is that what you mean?\n\nDoctor: Outside of arguments about the money, has this problem made it hard for you to work or manage your usual daily responsibilities?\n\nPatient: No, not really… I mean, aside from the money arguments, I still take care of my own meals and get myself to the county clinic and assistance appointments. I keep my things in order like I always have. So I think I’m managing okay… is that what you mean?\n\nDoctor: Has anyone told you that what you say is hard to follow or doesn’t make sense?\n\nPatient: I don’t think so… I mean, nobody has really told me I don’t make sense. Sometimes I worry I’m not explaining myself right, but I try to be clear. Is that okay?\n\nDoctor: Have you felt as if someone else was putting thoughts into your mind?\n\nPatient: No… I don’t think so. Like, my thoughts feel like mine. I haven’t noticed somebody putting them there or anything like that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?\n\nDoctor: Have you had a period when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?\n\nPatient: Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I get down sometimes, like anyone would, but I wouldn’t say most of the day nearly every day. At least, I haven’t noticed it like that. Is that alright?\n\nDoctor: Have you felt that other people could read your thoughts?\n\nPatient: I don’t think so… not like people can actually hear what I’m thinking. I might worry what people think of me sometimes, but I haven’t really felt like they can read my mind. Is that what you mean?\n\nDoctor: Have you seen things that other people could not see?\n\nPatient: Um… no, I don’t think so. Is that okay?\n\nDoctor: Has anyone said your behavior seems very odd or bizarre outside of the arguments about the money?\n\nPatient: No… I don’t think so. I don’t think people would say I’m acting bizarre, really.
